history.summary: A 999-year (quasi-freehold) 904sqft 2BR in D19 at $1383 psf — right at the project median — but a tiny boutique development with only 9 URA transactions and no MRT info, making it illiquid and its 4.2% appreciation unreliable. Quasi-freehold tenure is the one genuine plus.
history.rating_rationale: 999yr tenure functions like freehold and the 2BR/904sqft is a sensible efficient size at a reasonable $1.25M quantum. But this is a thin-data boutique: only 9 transactions (appreciation rate unreliable), no MRT proximity listed, and entry PSF is exactly at median (no discount cushion). Tenure is nice but doesn't offset the illiquidity and lack of a value or transit edge — Neutral.
red_flags: Only 9 URA transactions — thin, illiquid, appreciation rate unreliable
No MRT within useful distance (none listed) — weaker rental/resale draw
At-median PSF — no value discount to compensate for the illiquidity
catalysts: D19 NE growth corridor (PDD/CRL) as a regional tailwind

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Without nearby MRT, tenant demand leans on car/bus access — adequate for a Hillside/Upper Serangoon location but not a standout; 2BR format has the widest pool which helps.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: 4.2% rests on 9 txns — directionally OCR-plausible but statistically weak. Quasi-freehold tenure supports value retention but the boutique illiquidity is the limiter.
